Ethereum AquilaRouter 0x70d2473f911683fef696fb23ed25540e46d70734 only, a nonproxy immutable-factory direct AMM router; Sourcify runtime and creation grades are exact_match. Official current docs separately attribute Aquila to Rubicon as its maintained Uniswap V2 fork and list the exact router/factory. Rubicon is one new protocol, not a separate Aquila alias or a new Uniswap label.

Only source-bound direct token/native swaps and LP add/remove methods are admitted. No generic executor, opaque calldata, multicall, permit, approvals, wallet signing, bridge, Gladius intent signing, deprecated bathToken pool or orderbook admin surface is admitted. The app also aggregates other systems; this does not admit API-generated or app-generated calldata wholesale.

Factory is immutable 0x7bad585c3ae4ae266f92a4af13b388bc7b26067c and WETH is immutable 0xc02aaa39b223fe8d0a0e5c4f27ead9083c756cc2, corroborated by reads. Pair addresses are deterministic CREATE2 results of this factory, sorted tokens and hardcoded init-code hash 0x79cb29831f0abd24ae48de6fa5dc9eb647f10df38618ed09b70b2044d35dfba5. Token addresses and path are fixed financial data, not arbitrary target-plus-calldata execution. Swap callbacks always receive empty bytes.

Token and LP amounts use their own native decimals, ETH uses wei. All calls check deadline >= block.timestamp. Token inputs and LP tokens are pulled from msg.sender under preexisting allowances; no third-party payer parameter exists. to controls financial output/LP recipient. Nonpayable calls require zero native value; payable methods use msg.value as ETH input/budget.

Exact-input swaps enforce output minimum; exact-output swaps enforce token input maximum or msg.value budget. AquilaLibrary applies amountIn*997 against reserveIn*1000 (0.3% per-hop fee), floors exact-input output and divides then adds one for exact-output input. Paths require at least two tokens in normal quote paths; ETH routes require WETH at the corresponding endpoint. Token behavior, reserves and recipient handling can still cause reversion or loss.

addLiquidity may create a new pair, sends only reserve-ratio-adjusted caller tokens, then mints pair shares to to. Initial empty pool uses both desired inputs directly without testing amount minima; for an existing pool the optimized opposite side is minimum-checked. addLiquidityETH wraps only required ETH and refunds excess to msg.sender. LP shares/principal/yield and a complete exit path are not guaranteed.

removeLiquidity pulls caller LP into the pair and burns to to, then checks nominal token minima. ETH variants route through this router, unwrap WETH and pay to. Fee-on-transfer removal forwards the router entire token balance and its token minimum is checked on nominal pair burn amounts, not actual receiver balance; it is not a guaranteed post-tax minimum.

Fee-on-transfer exact-input swaps compute each hop input from actual pair token balance minus stored reserve. Token-output variants enforce the final recipient balance increase minimum; ETH-output variant unwraps the router entire WETH balance and checks that amount. These variants can sweep preexisting router dust; the router is not user-segregated custody and users should not prefund it. Normal exact-output and liquidity paths do not promise fee-on-transfer compatibility.

The applicable router, library and interfaces are preserved in full. No independent persistent runtime attestation, token safety or solvency proof is made for every factory/pair/WETH/token dependency; pair implementation financial mechanics are represented by the exact bound router interface and source calls. Native refunds/payments can fail if caller/recipient cannot receive ETH; callbacks and arbitrary program execution remain unadmitted.

Official current docs separately attribute Aquila to Rubicon as its maintained Uniswap V2 fork and list the exact router/factory. Rubicon is one new protocol, not a separate Aquila alias or a new Uniswap label.

Only source-bound direct token/native swaps and LP add/remove methods are admitted. No generic executor, opaque calldata, multicall, permit, approvals, wallet signing, bridge, Gladius intent signing, deprecated bathToken pool or orderbook admin surface is admitted. The app also aggregates other systems; this does not admit API-generated or app-generated calldata wholesale.

Factory is immutable 0x7bad585c3ae4ae266f92a4af13b388bc7b26067c and WETH is immutable 0xc02aaa39b223fe8d0a0e5c4f27ead9083c756cc2, corroborated by reads. Pair addresses are deterministic CREATE2 results of this factory, sorted tokens and hardcoded init-code hash 0x79cb29831f0abd24ae48de6fa5dc9eb647f10df38618ed09b70b2044d35dfba5. Token addresses and path are fixed financial data, not arbitrary target-plus-calldata execution. Swap callbacks always receive empty bytes.

Token and LP amounts use their own native decimals, ETH uses wei. All calls check deadline >= block.timestamp. Token inputs and LP tokens are pulled from msg.sender under preexisting allowances; no third-party payer parameter exists. to controls financial output/LP recipient. Nonpayable calls require zero native value; payable methods use msg.value as ETH input/budget.

Exact-input swaps enforce output minimum; exact-output swaps enforce token input maximum or msg.value budget. AquilaLibrary applies amountIn*997 against reserveIn*1000 (0.3% per-hop fee), floors exact-input output and divides then adds one for exact-output input. Paths require at least two tokens in normal quote paths; ETH routes require WETH at the corresponding endpoint. Token behavior, reserves and recipient handling can still cause reversion or loss.

addLiquidity may create a new pair, sends only reserve-ratio-adjusted caller tokens, then mints pair shares to to. Initial empty pool uses both desired inputs directly without testing amount minima; for an existing pool the optimized opposite side is minimum-checked. addLiquidityETH wraps only required ETH and refunds excess to msg.sender. LP shares/principal/yield and a complete exit path are not guaranteed.

removeLiquidity pulls caller LP into the pair and burns to to, then checks nominal token minima. ETH variants route through this router, unwrap WETH and pay to. Fee-on-transfer removal forwards the router entire token balance and its token minimum is checked on nominal pair burn amounts, not actual receiver balance; it is not a guaranteed post-tax minimum.

Fee-on-transfer exact-input swaps compute each hop input from actual pair token balance minus stored reserve. Token-output variants enforce the final recipient balance increase minimum; ETH-output variant unwraps the router entire WETH balance and checks that amount. These variants can sweep preexisting router dust; the router is not user-segregated custody and users should not prefund it. Normal exact-output and liquidity paths do not promise fee-on-transfer compatibility.

The applicable router, library and interfaces are preserved in full. No independent persistent runtime attestation, token safety or solvency proof is made for every factory/pair/WETH/token dependency; pair implementation financial mechanics are represented by the exact bound router interface and source calls. Native refunds/payments can fail if caller/recipient cannot receive ETH; callbacks and arbitrary program execution remain unadmitted.

Initial empty pool uses both desired inputs directly without testing amount minima; for an existing pool the optimized opposite side is minimum-checked. addLiquidityETH wraps only required ETH and refunds excess to msg.sender. LP shares/principal/yield and a complete exit path are not guaranteed.

removeLiquidity pulls caller LP into the pair and burns to to, then checks nominal token minima. ETH variants route through this router, unwrap WETH and pay to. Fee-on-transfer removal forwards the router entire token balance and its token minimum is checked on nominal pair burn amounts, not actual receiver balance; it is not a guaranteed post-tax minimum.

Fee-on-transfer exact-input swaps compute each hop input from actual pair token balance minus stored reserve. Token-output variants enforce the final recipient balance increase minimum; ETH-output variant unwraps the router entire WETH balance and checks that amount. These variants can sweep preexisting router dust; the router is not user-segregated custody and users should not prefund it. Normal exact-output and liquidity paths do not promise fee-on-transfer compatibility.

The applicable router, library and interfaces are preserved in full. No independent persistent runtime attestation, token safety or solvency proof is made for every factory/pair/WETH/token dependency; pair implementation financial mechanics are represented by the exact bound router interface and source calls. Native refunds/payments can fail if caller/recipient cannot receive ETH; callbacks and arbitrary program execution remain unadmitted.

What is Rubicon?

Rubicon is an open trading platform for ERC-20 (opens in a new tab) tokens. We believe that all of the world's financial assets will be tokenized; Rubicon is the central hub where they can trade in an efficient, transparent, and trustless fashion.

Rubicon is designed to offer efficient ERC-20 trading infrastructure for traders, market makers, projects, and integrators. Traders get access to onchain markets and routes, while liquidity providers and market makers get flexible tools for creating and managing liquidity.

Trade tokens on the Rubicon App (opens in a new tab) with swaps, market orders, limit-order style flows, and cross-chain routing through swap.

Protocol Overview

Rubicon integrates several trading mechanisms into one liquidity stack:

  1. Rubicon CLMM - a Uniswap V3 fork for concentrated-liquidity markets.
  2. Rubicon Aquila - a constant-product AMM based on the Uniswap V2 model.
  3. Rubicon Gladius - an intent-based trading and execution system with API-driven market-maker workflows.
  4. Rubicon Classic - Rubicon's fully onchain order book system.
  5. Rubicon HFT Vaults - a Gamma Strategies V1 Hypervisor fork for managed CLMM liquidity.

By combining concentrated liquidity, managed vault liquidity, AMM liquidity, offchain order intent, and onchain order book infrastructure, Rubicon can support many styles of ERC-20 trading without requiring users or integrators to treat them as separate venues.

Rubicon Stack

Rubicon CLMM

Rubicon CLMM is a fork of Uniswap V3. LPs choose active price ranges, and traders route through concentrated liquidity around market prices.

Rubicon Aquila

Aquila is Rubicon's constant-product AMM based on the Uniswap V2 model. It provides simple onchain pool liquidity for routes and integrations.

Rubicon Gladius

Gladius pairs offchain efficiency with onchain settlement, decentralization, and transparency. Order intents are encoded and matched offchain, then settled onchain through Rubicon contracts. This enables efficient, gasless, non-custodial flows for traders and market makers.

Developers integrating Gladius can also review the Gladius API, Gladius SDK, and filler integration guide.

Rubicon Classic

Classic is Rubicon's fully onchain order book system. It supports direct limit-order style liquidity and remains available for integrators and market makers that need CLOB-style markets.

The Classic layer includes RubiconMarket, the core order book contract, and RubiconRouter, which routes token swaps and supports multi-hop swaps when two tokens do not have a direct underlying order book.

Rubicon HFT Vaults

HFT Vaults are a fork of Gamma Strategies V1's Hypervisor system. They let depositors supply paired assets to CLMM vaults while a trusted market maker manages active ranges.

Browse vaults in the Rubicon App (opens in a new tab).

Why is this important?

One of crypto's core promises is an open financial system, but much of crypto trading still depends on centralized exchanges and closed infrastructure. Those systems custody user funds, charge opaque fees, and are not always aligned with their users.

Rubicon brings trading infrastructure onchain. The goal is open markets where users keep custody, contracts are verifiable, and liquidity can be built and accessed transparently.

Aquila

Aquila is a fork of Uniswap V2. It provides constant-product AMM liquidity for ERC-20 swaps, routes, and integrations.

The model is simple: liquidity providers deposit token pairs, traders swap against pooled liquidity, and prices move according to the pool reserves. Aquila is useful where markets need straightforward pooled liquidity without concentrated ranges or custom order flow.
